spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The mathematical tension is between a sharply specified conjectural moment scale, supported by two different heuristic formalisms, and the very small set of exponents for which a full asymptotic is known. Broad lower bounds preserve the predicted order from below, so the missing object is effective one-sided control from above rather than another guess for the scale.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: The unit defines M_k(T) as the integral of |ζ(1/2+it)|^{2k}, records the conjecture M_k(T) asymptotic to C_k T(log T)^{k^2}, and notes agreement between random-matrix and multiple-Dirichlet-series predictions, including lower-order refinements. Full asymptotics are stated only for k=1 and k=2, while lower bounds of the conjectured logarithmic order are known for wider classes of k, with some extensions conditional on RH.
directed.conceptual_reading: A precise conjecture can expose a target scale without supplying a proof mechanism. The source reframes progress as closing a one-sided gap: existing lower bounds certify that the proposed scale is not too large, whereas an upper bound must suppress rare large values.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The moment family M_k(T) compresses the value distribution of ζ on the critical line into an exponent-indexed scale. Random-matrix constants and multiple Dirichlet series are independent conjectural representations that converge on the same leading prediction; lower bounds bridge that prediction to proved partial evidence.
directed.boundary_or_failure: Nothing in this span derives an upper bound or an asymptotic beyond k=1,2. Agreement of conjectural frameworks and matching lower bounds does not establish the upper side, and analogous family conjectures are only announced here.
directed.uncertainty: The prose and qualitative hierarchy are clear, but displayed exponents and comparison symbols are extraction-sensitive; the reading relies only on the legible k^2 scale and stated conditionality.

supported: The span defines M_k(T), states the conjectural C_k T(log T)^{k^2} scale, and names the random-matrix and multiple-Dirichlet-series routes to the same conjecture.
It supports asymptotics only for k=1,2 and lower bounds for broader k-classes, with the all-positive-real statement explicitly conditional on RH.
inference: The contrast between proved lower bounds and scarce asymptotics, together with the bounded following context announcing upper bounds, supports describing an unresolved upper-side gap.
Viewing the moment family as a distributional compression is a reasonable interpretation rather than a quoted claim.
unsupported_or_imported: Calling the two conjectural approaches independent is stronger than the span's statement that the second is alternative.
The claim that an upper bound must suppress rare large values imports the later large-value reduction; this span does not supply that mechanism.

The Euler coefficients make the square layer contribute a negative half-log-log bias, so the orthogonal family is centered below zero and the resulting moment exponent changes accordingly.

Powers of degree at least three contribute O(1), while the prime-square terms contribute asymptotically minus one half log log x. Centering the large-value event at V-one half log log X and applying the analogous family argument yields moderate and large tail estimates and an upper moment bound with orthogonal exponent k(k-1)/2, up to ε.
directed.conceptual_reading: Symmetry type is detected by the coherent mean of the square layer rather than by changing the entire proof architecture. The sign reversal changes the center while leaving the fluctuation-control mechanism recognizable.

directed.boundary_or_failure: This is a structural method sketch, not a complete proof. It is conditional, formula-sensitive, and does not say that every twist is small or that the Gaussian prediction follows from the upper-tail estimate.
directed.uncertainty: The negative half-log-log contribution and orthogonal exponent are supported by the prose and dossier, but Euler-factor displays, signs, and exact threshold formulas require scan verification.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The three family cases compress into a common Gaussian-fluctuation picture whose center is read from prime-square mass: zero for unitary, positive for symplectic, and negative for orthogonal families. The remaining obstruction is spectral—zeros very near the central point prevent the one-sided upper-bound method from becoming a full Selberg-type distribution theorem.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: The source presents Keating-Snaith predictions that log central L-values are Gaussian: unitary characters have mean zero and variance about one half log log q; quadratic Dirichlet values have positive mean about one half log log|d| and variance about log log|d|; positive-sign elliptic-curve twists have negative mean about one half log log|d| and comparable variance. It says the paper's ideas, under GRH, give a Gaussian-tail upper bound for fixed standardized deviations. Recovering the full Selberg analogues additionally requires that most family members have no zero very near 1/2.
directed.conceptual_reading: Center and fluctuation are distinct structural components. Prime squares predict the center shift, while prime-level variation supplies a broadly common variance scale; nearby central zeros are information not controlled by this one-sided representation and therefore mark the barrier to a two-sided distribution statement.
directed.representation_or_bridge: Standardizing log|L| by its family-dependent mean and variance places the three symmetry types in one comparison frame. The zero-avoidance condition is the missing bridge from upper-tail control to a full Gaussian limit.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The Gaussian distributions are conjectural, the fixed-deviation result is only an upper bound conditional on GRH, and the stronger analogue needs an extra hypothesis about near-central zeros. Orthogonal statements also restrict to positive functional-equation sign because negative sign forces the central value to vanish.
directed.uncertainty: The signs and family ordering of the centers and the zero-proximity obstruction are clear; exact mean and variance constants are OCR-sensitive.

supported: The span explicitly presents conjectural Gaussian laws with mean zero for the unitary family, positive mean for the symplectic family, and negative mean for positive-sign orthogonal twists, together with their variance scales.
It states a GRH-conditional Gaussian-tail upper bound for fixed standardized deviations and requires an additional no-near-central-zero condition for Selberg-type analogues.
The positive-sign restriction and forced central vanishing for the other sign are explicit.
inference: Separating family-dependent centers from broadly comparable fluctuation scales and identifying near-central zeros as the barrier to the stronger conclusion are supported interpretations.
unsupported_or_imported: The exact span does not attribute the three center shifts to prime-square mass, so that causal synthesis is imported from preceding units or dossier material.
The claim that prime-level variation supplies the common variance is likewise absent from this span.
paraphrase_or_style_risk: The phrase one-sided representation is underspecified here; the span states an upper-tail result and an added zero hypothesis but does not name a representation.
context_or_ocr_risk: Mean and variance constants and the normal-tail display are OCR-sensitive, while their signs, ordering, and logical status remain clear.
revision_instructions: Retain the three conjectural family laws, fixed-deviation upper-bound status, sign restriction, and extra zero-avoidance hypothesis; remove the prime-square and prime-level causal attributions unless explicitly linked to their supporting earlier spans.
